title: Peripheral Atherectomy and Angioplasty for Lower Extremity Arterial Disease
description: Medicare coverage criteria for percutaneous peripheral atherectomy and angioplasty. Requires documented chronic lifestyle-limiting intermittent claudication (Rutherford Category 3) or critical limb ischemia (Rutherford 4-6) with non-healing ulcers, failure of >= 3 months supervised exercise therapy, and documented arterial stenosis >= 70%.

criteria.name: Severe Claudication (Rutherford 3) or Critical Limb Ischemia (Rutherford 4-6)
criteria.description: Clinical documentation of severe intermittent claudication severely limiting ambulation (Rutherford Category 3) or critical limb ischemia with rest pain / ischemic ulceration.
criteria.clinical_intent: Clinical severity threshold for invasive intervention
criteria.source_text_excerpt: The major manifestations of chronic ischemia are ischemic rest pain, ischemic ulceration, and gangrene.

criteria.name: Arterial Hemodynamic Stenosis (>= 70% on Angiography or ABI <= 0.70)
criteria.description: Non-invasive vascular testing showing Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) <= 0.70 and angiography/duplex showing >= 70% stenosis of target lower extremity artery.
criteria.clinical_intent: Hemodynamic proof of severe arterial obstruction
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Detection of PAD in most patients is accomplished through history, physical examination, and resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) for LEs or wrist-brachial index (WBI) for UEs.

criteria.name: Mild Claudication or Asymptomatic PAD Exclusion
criteria.description: Invasive revascularization performed for mild claudication (Rutherford Category 1 or 2) without prior trial of supervised exercise.
criteria.clinical_intent: Exclude premature interventional therapy for mild disease
criteria.source_text_excerpt: This guideline defines 4 clinical subsets of PAD: asymptomatic PAD (may have functional impairment), chronic symptomatic PAD (claudication), CLTI, and ALI.
